title: Pokémon Fans Queue Overnight for Limited-Edition Stamps in Taipei
summaryZh: 寶可夢限量郵票開賣，粉絲徹夜排隊，中華郵政道歉。
summaryHi: ताइपे में सीमित संस्करण वाले पोकेमॉन डाक टिकटों के लिए प्रशंसक रात भर कतार में रहे।
summaryEs: Fans de Pokémon hacen cola toda la noche en Taipéi por sellos de edición limitada.
summaryJa: ポケモン限定切手の発売に徹夜の行列、中華郵政が謝罪。
summaryKo: 포켓몬 한정판 우표에 팬들 밤샘 줄서기, 중화우정 사과.
summaryEn: Fans queued overnight in Taipei for limited-edition Pokémon stamps; Chunghwa Post apologised for the long waits.
paragraphs: Pokémon fans formed queues stretching hundreds of meters at the Taipei World Trade Center on Friday, with some camping out overnight to get their hands on limited-edition stamps released by Chunghwa Post.

The stamps and co-branded merchandise are being sold at PHILATAIPEI 2026, an international stamp exhibition. However, only a fifth of the stock was set aside for on-site buyers. Sixty percent had already gone to online pre-orders, and the remaining twenty percent was shared among selected post offices across the country.

Organisers handed out 1,200 queue tickets for the complete Pokémon set and another 500 for stamps and individual items ahead of the 11 o'clock start. First in line for the stamps was a fan surnamed Wang, who had headed to the venue straight after finishing her shift on Thursday, armed with a Pikachu blanket and a budget of around 2,000 Taiwan dollars.

Chunghwa Post chairman Wang Kwo-tsai admitted that turnout and orders had far exceeded expectations and apologised to everyone who had queued. He said the company would review its stock levels and sales arrangements and consider a second Pokémon release. The current items, however, cannot be restocked because of contractual limits.
The exhibition runs until November 25, and admission is free.
Many people in Taipei waited in long lines on Friday. They wanted to buy special Pokémon stamps. Some fans waited all night.
The stamps are from Chunghwa Post, Taiwan's post office. They are sold at a big stamp show called PHILATAIPEI 2026. The show is at the Taipei World Trade Center.
The lines were hundreds of meters long before the sale started at 11 a.m. The first woman in line had a Pikachu blanket. She wanted to spend about 2,000 Taiwan dollars.
The head of Chunghwa Post said sorry to the people who waited. Many more people came than he expected. The post office will not make more of these Pokémon things.
The show is open until November 25. It is free to go in.
sentZh: 週五，台北有很多人排了很長的隊。
他們想買特別的寶可夢郵票。
有些粉絲等了一整晚。
這些郵票來自台灣的郵局中華郵政。
它們在一個叫做「2026台北國際郵展」的大型郵票展上販售。
展覽在台北世界貿易中心舉行。
在早上11點開賣前，隊伍長達數百公尺。
排第一位的女士帶著皮卡丘毯子。
她打算花大約新台幣2,000元。
中華郵政的負責人向等待的人道歉。
來的人比他預期的多很多。
郵局不會再製作更多這些寶可夢商品。
展覽開放到11月25日。
免費入場。

paragraphs: Hundreds of Pokémon fans queued outside the Taipei World Trade Center on Friday, and some even waited overnight, to buy limited-edition stamps from Chunghwa Post.

The stamps and other Pokémon products are on sale at PHILATAIPEI 2026, an international stamp exhibition. Sixty percent of the items were sold online in advance, twenty percent at post offices around Taiwan, and only twenty percent at the exhibition itself.

The post office gave out 1,200 queue tickets for the full Pokémon set and 500 for stamps and single items. Before sales began at 11 a.m., the lines stretched for hundreds of meters. The first person in line, a woman surnamed Wang, came straight after work on Thursday with a Pikachu blanket.

Chunghwa Post chairman Wang Kwo-tsai said far more people came than expected, and he apologised to those who had waited. The company will review how it sells products like these. Because of the contract, the Pokémon items will not be restocked.
The exhibition runs until November 25, and entry is free.

這些郵票和其他寶可夢商品在國際郵票展「2026台北國際郵展」上販售。
六成商品已提前在網路上賣出，兩成在全台郵局販售，只有兩成在展場現場販售。
郵局發出1,200張全套寶可夢商品的號碼牌，以及500張郵票和單品的號碼牌。
上午11點開賣前，隊伍綿延數百公尺。
排在第一位的是一位王姓女子，她週四下班後直接帶著皮卡丘毯子前來。
中華郵政董事長王國材說，來的人遠遠超出預期，他向排隊等候的民眾道歉。
公司將檢討這類商品的販售方式。
由於合約關係，寶可夢商品不會補貨。
展覽持續到11月25日，免費入場。

paragraphs: Devoted Pokémon fans turned the entrance of the Taipei World Trade Center into a makeshift campsite on Friday, with queues snaking for hundreds of meters as collectors waited, in some cases overnight, for a chance to buy limited-edition stamps issued by Chunghwa Post.

The stamps, along with an array of co-branded merchandise, are the star attraction at PHILATAIPEI 2026, an international philatelic exhibition. Yet those who turned up in person were competing for a modest share of the stock: sixty percent had been allocated to online presales and twenty percent to designated post offices nationwide, leaving just a fifth for on-site sales.

Ahead of the 11 o'clock opening, staff distributed 1,200 queue tickets for the full Pokémon collection and 500 for stamps and individual items. At the front of the stamp queue was a fan surnamed Wang, who had gone directly to the venue after her Thursday shift, wrapped in a Pikachu blanket and prepared to spend roughly 2,000 Taiwan dollars.

Chunghwa Post chairman Wang Kwo-tsai conceded that both attendance and orders had vastly outstripped projections and expressed regret to those left waiting. The company, he said, would reassess quantities and sales logistics and weigh up a further Pokémon issue, although contractual restrictions rule out restocking the current range.
The exhibition continues until November 25, with free admission.
sentZh: 週五，死忠寶可夢粉絲把台北世界貿易中心入口變成臨時營地，隊伍蜿蜒數百公尺，收藏家們有些甚至徹夜等待，只為有機會買到中華郵政發行的限量版郵票。
這些郵票連同一系列聯名商品，是國際集郵展「2026台北國際郵展」的最大亮點。
然而親自到場的人只能爭搶一小部分庫存：六成分配給網路預售，兩成給全國指定郵局，現場販售只剩五分之一。
在11點開門前，工作人員發出1,200張全套寶可夢收藏的號碼牌，以及500張郵票和單品號碼牌。
郵票隊伍最前面的是一位王姓粉絲，她週四下班後直接到會場，裹著皮卡丘毯子，準備花大約新台幣2,000元。
中華郵政董事長王國材承認，到場人數和訂單都大大超出預估，並向久候的民眾致歉。
他說公司將重新評估數量和銷售流程，並考慮再推出一波寶可夢商品，但合約限制使目前的系列無法補貨。
展覽持續到11月25日，免費入場。

paragraphs: Long queues formed outside the Taipei World Trade Center on Friday as enthusiastic Pokémon fans, some of whom had waited overnight, competed to purchase limited-edition stamps produced by Chunghwa Post, Taiwan's postal service.

The stamps and related co-branded products are being sold at PHILATAIPEI 2026, an international stamp exhibition. The distribution of stock, however, left relatively little for visitors: sixty percent was reserved for online pre-orders and a further twenty percent for designated post offices, meaning that only one fifth was available at the venue.

Before sales commenced at 11 a.m., staff issued 1,200 queue tickets for the complete Pokémon set and 500 for stamps and individual items. The first person in the stamp queue, a woman surnamed Wang, had travelled to the venue immediately after her work shift on Thursday, bringing a Pikachu blanket and intending to spend approximately 2,000 Taiwan dollars.

Chunghwa Post's chairman, Wang Kwo-tsai, acknowledged that demand had been considerably greater than anticipated and apologised to those who had queued. He stated that the company would evaluate its stock levels and sales procedures and would consider launching another Pokémon series. Owing to contractual restrictions, though, the existing products will not be restocked.
The exhibition is open to the public free of charge until November 25.
sentZh: 週五，熱情的寶可夢粉絲在台北世界貿易中心外排起長龍，其中有些人徹夜等候，爭相購買台灣郵政機構中華郵政推出的限量版郵票。
這些郵票和相關聯名產品在國際郵票展「2026台北國際郵展」上販售。
然而庫存分配讓現場訪客能買到的相對較少：六成保留給網路預購，另外兩成給指定郵局，也就是說只有五分之一在會場販售。
上午11點開賣前，工作人員發出1,200張全套寶可夢商品號碼牌，以及500張郵票和單品號碼牌。
郵票隊伍的第一位是一位王姓女子，她週四下班後立刻前往會場，帶著皮卡丘毯子，打算花大約新台幣2,000元。
中華郵政董事長王國材承認需求遠比預期還大，並向排隊的民眾道歉。
他表示公司將評估庫存量和銷售程序，並考慮推出另一個寶可夢系列。
不過，由於合約限制，現有產品不會補貨。
展覽免費對外開放至11月25日。
